**RULED BY hv 2026-08-19, REPLACING THE TWO-REGION DESIGN. `.intentfiles` IS DURABLE STATE: THE RECORD OF WHICH DATABASE ARTEFACTS ALSO HAVE A REALISED FORM ON DISK.** **THE ARCHITECTURE IN ONE LINE, hv's: REALISATION IS DRIVEN FROM `.intentfiles`; COMMANDS CHANGE `.intentfiles`; `organize` REALISES IT.** **_AUTHORED_ WAS vc's WORD AND IT IS WRONG -- hv corrected it before anyone built on it.** It is NOT _never touched by an intent command_: **`st new` ADDS the id, `st done` REMOVES it, `st hydrate`/`st dehydrate` and the ISSUE equivalents do it directly, and a human may edit it by hand.** **THE ONE THING THAT CHANGED FROM THE TWO-REGION DESIGN IS THAT NOTHING RECOMPUTES IT.** There is no derivation from status that overwrites what is there, which is why the protected region is unnecessary: **a write is a CHANGE TO STATE, never a REGENERATION OF IT.** hv: _why isn't the organise operation simply: a) look at .intentfiles, b) hydrate the items in the file, c) dehydrate any previously hydrated items that are no longer in the file._ **THE TWO REGIONS EXISTED ONLY BECAUSE THE FILE WAS MACHINE-GENERATED: if `organize` rewrote the list from status every run, a hand-added line would be wiped, so a protected region was needed. Remove the regeneration and the protected region has nothing to protect against.** **IT ALSO EXPLAINS WHY `intentfiles::render` HAD NO CALLER: the thing it does is not needed.** No function of status, no negative pin, one writer, one source of truth. **THE LIFECYCLE VERBS EDIT THE LIST AS PART OF THE TRANSITION, AND A CLOSING VERB WARNS BEFORE DEHYDRATING OVER UNSYNCED WORK.** `st new` does not add the entry (hv, 2026-08-27: a thread is created at `triage`, which is not the realised set), and neither does `st new --dehydrate`; `st start`, `st resume` and `st reopen` add it; `st done`, `st fc`, `st cancel`, `st hold` and `st triage` remove it; `st reinstate` leaves it alone because it lands on `not-started`; `st hydrate` / `st dehydrate` / the ISSUE equivalents add and remove it directly. **`st done --keep` closes the artefact WITHOUT removing the entry.** **vc 2026-08-19, CORRECTING ITS OWN WORDING ON dc's TRACE: THE CLOSING VERBS DO NOT DELETE FILES, SO THE `REFUSE` CLAUSE IS WITHDRAWN.** `organize.rs:695` is the only line in the tool that removes an estate file. vc measured all 7 delete sites in `crates/*/src/`: the other six are `write_set`'s own rollback (4), `install`'s temp dir, and `backup::prune` -- which dc's enumeration missed and which is safe by a guard rather than by not existing, being confined to the snapshot directory by a `starts_with` check and only ever removing files it holds a row for. **`st done` and `st cancel` change DB state and the list; the realiser makes disk match; nothing else deletes anything.** **SO THE CLOSING VERBS WARN, NAMING THE PATHS, WHEN THE ARTEFACT HOLDS ON-DISK BYTES THE STORE HAS NEVER SEEN -- THEY DO NOT REFUSE, AND THEY ARE NOT A SECOND AUTHORITY OVER DELETION.** `Facade::sync_uncommitted` (AC-03.5) answers a question the realiser's gate does not -- _are there bytes here nobody has synced_ -- and asking it at the moment of closing puts that answer in front of the operator then, rather than at the next `organize` when they have moved on. **A SECOND GATE WOULD BE WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY DIVERGENT COPY: the two gates answer DIFFERENT questions, so they would disagree BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by drift, and a gate refusing on a different question than the one governing the destructive act refuses work the real authority would allow.** The refusal keeps its one home in the realiser's per-file gate, which already declines three ways: any byte difference on re-render; `AttachmentDiverged` reported with both remedies and neither side touched; and an attachment the store has never seen left `Unclaimed` and never removed.

**STALE CLAUSE CLEARED 2026-08-20 (vc), BEFORE ic BUILDS TO IT. THE TWO REFERENCES TO _the ISSUE equivalents_ ABOVE ARE VOID.** hv's ruling 1 dropped `ISSUE:` from the `.intentfiles` grammar and ic landed it at `d855ea1f`; `Sigil::Issue` no longer exists and the grammar is `STEELTHREAD` alone. **So the verb set this criterion governs is the STEEL-THREAD set only** -- `st new` / `st new --dehydrate`, `st done` / `st done --keep`, `st cancel`, `st reopen`, `st reinstate`, `st hydrate`, `st dehydrate` -- and `issues hydrate` / `issues dehydrate` edit no manifest because there is no sigil for them to write. **NOT A CHANGE OF INTENT, A CHANGE OF ARITY**: every clause about WHAT the lifecycle verbs do to the list stands exactly as written; only the population they range over narrowed. **Recorded rather than deleted, because a clause that was true when written and was voided by a later ruling is the fifth instance of that shape this estate met today** -- a needle, a guard, a roster, a success message and now a criterion, none of which reported anything when their subject moved.

**AND THE REMOVAL PRIMITIVE IS IN SCOPE (ic's question, answered):** if the closing verbs remove an entry, there must be something that removes one, so an `unpin` beside `pin` is an implementation consequence of this criterion rather than an addition to it. **The WARNING stays a warning**: the `REFUSE` clause is withdrawn above and is not reinstated by the removal primitive existing.

**`st cancel --keep` IS IN SCOPE AND ALWAYS WAS (hv ruling 2026-08-20, on ic's question; canon clause added by vc). This criterion named `st done --keep` and said nothing about `st cancel`, so the surface shipped an override on ONE of two identical acts.** ic guessed the asymmetry was deliberate -- cancelling being the stronger statement -- and **hv ruled the opposite, for a reason worth keeping: `--keep` is not about how sure you are that the work is over, it is about whether you still need to READ the files, and a cancelled thread is at least as likely to be one you are still mining for what it decided.** Built and green: the flag on `st cancel` in the table and the `.md` face, `Facade::st_cancel_listing`, the render arm, and **two tests -- one for the verb and one asserting the two verbs AGREE**, because a single test cannot show agreement and an override present on one of two identical acts had already diverged once.
